title: Add onboard quickprober and changelog conciliator
author: Lina Park
description:
Context and motivation: onboarding frequently requires two manual steps that slow releases: (1) quick runtime sanity sampling to validate that a packed/quantized variant stays within latency/quality tolerances, and (2) a human-curated changelog draft that summarizes key perf/accuracy deltas. This PR adds a lightweight 'quickprober' runner that executes targeted micro-benchmarks against new onboard artifacts and a 'changelog conciliator' service that synthesizes compact release drafts from the probe outputs and metadata diffs.

High-level design: quickprober runs a configurable suite of probes (latency microbench, top-k token divergence, sample prompts from the model intake manifest) constrained to 60s per variant and emits a compact probe-tape (JSONL). The conciliator ingests the probe-tape plus the model's onboarding metadata delta (profile, tokenizer fingerprint, quantization flags) and produces a one-paragraph changelog, a breakdown of impact buckets (latency, token-cost, accuracy-signals), and suggested rollout tags (canary/gradual/fallback). Both components are implemented to be idempotent, signable, and compatible with existing onboard pipeline hooks.

What this PR does (single-string checklist): - Adds quickprober binary and test harness integrated with onboard CI; - Implements conciliator microservice and a local CLI for previewing drafts; - Adds a signed probe-tape schema and a small provenance ledger entry on successful probes; - Introduces a reconciler that compares newly generated changelogs with previous release blurb and surfaces substantive diffs; - Adds unit and integration tests covering probe stability, conciliator grammar scaffolding, and signature verification; - Updates onboarding docs and the release automation README with usage and rollback guidance.

Operational notes and constraints: quickprober defaults to conservative probe budgets and will not run heavy evals — teams can opt into extended suites. Probe outputs are stored in the internal artifacts bucket with a short TTL; conciliator stores a draft in the model-profile release_notes field but marks drafts as 'auto-draft' until a reviewer signs off. Security: probe results and drafts are written with existing KMS envelopes; conciliator verifies artifact signatures before accepting probe-tapes.

Migration steps: existing onboard pipelines will pick up the quickprober step automatically if the model manifest includes "quickprobe: true". For models without the flag, the conciliator can be invoked manually via CLI or the onboarding web UI.

Rollback: the reconciler adds a short rollback suggestion when latency or divergence exceed configured thresholds. The onboarding pipeline will still require human approval for any release that the conciliator marks as 'high-impact'.

Why this is different from prior work: prior PRs focused on full-scale profiling and release note generation. This patch purposely targets a low-latency, low-cost sampling surface that fits the fast path of onboarding and produces concise, machine-readable changelogs suitable for automated tagging and later expansion.
